deck.request: Is Harbour Credit Union growing safely, and how does it compare with its regional peers?
deck.brief: Is Harbour Credit Union growing safely against its regional peers?
deck.answer: Harbour is growing faster than its peers on thinner liquidity, so funding comes before further lending.

pages.title: Harbour is growing faster than its peers on thinner liquidity
pages.why: The opening states the answer and the three findings behind it, each with what it means for the plan

settles.what: growth, cash generation and liquidity cover against seven regional peers

pages.adds: Each point carries what its finding means for the plan, which the table does not show
points: Lending is outrunning the funding behind it. Earnings no longer pay for the growth, so each new loan now draws on wholesale money or on the liquid assets that cover what falls due within a year.

One more year at this pace, funded the same way, breaches the cover floor. The board therefore has to choose between slowing lending and raising term deposits before the next budget, and funding comes before further lending.

The efficiency gain is real and did not come from shrinking the network, so there is no case for closures. Against its peers Harbour leads on growth, not on margin, which makes the price of new funding the number to protect.
The peer comparison rests on one year of regulatory returns, and one union publishes no capital ratio, so the ranking is a guide to position rather than a forecast.

pages.title: Loans grew 57% in seven years to 648 million
pages.why: The growth of the book over time is the claim, so the series is drawn

settles.what: loan book at year end FY19 to FY26

pages.bar: A loan book this much larger needs deposits, wholesale funding and regulatory capital that have grown at the same pace, which the next pages test

pages.title: Profit rose again while operating cash flow fell 21%
pages.why: Two year-on-year movements set against the cash series that produced one of them

settles.what: profit after tax and operating cash flow, FY25 to FY26

exhibit.heading: Operating cash flow
exhibit.caption: Operating cash flow fell to 66 million in FY26, the first decline in five years, while profit after tax rose to 49 million: growth in lending absorbed the cash that earnings produced

pages.title: The liquidity cushion narrowed from 41 million to 8 million
pages.why: The gap between two series in one unit is the claim, so both are drawn on one scale

settles.what: liquid assets and short-term liabilities at year end

exhibit.heading: Liquid assets and liabilities due within a year

pages.bar: Another year of lending at this pace, funded the same way, would take liquid assets below the liabilities that fall due within a year

pages.title: Costs fell nine points without closing branches
pages.why: A ratio and a count in different units, each read on its own panel
pages.adds: The captions say the efficiency gain did not come from shrinking the network

exhibits.heading: Cost-to-income ratio
exhibits.caption: The ratio fell from 71 to 62 percent over seven years of rising income

exhibits.heading: Branches open at year end

basis.relevance: It rules out branch closures as the source of the cost saving

exhibits.caption: The network lost two branches in seven years, far too few to explain the saving

pages.title: Harbour ranks fourth of eight on net interest margin
pages.why: The whole peer set on one measure, with the subject marked

settles.what: net interest margin across eight credit unions, FY26

pages.bar: Loan growth, not margin, is where Harbour leads its seven regional peers, so the plan protects the cost of funding before it adds lending
